Tested wasmtime v47.0.2 with OpenVINO 2026.1 on a bare metal SPR system with Windows Server 2025. The workload runs fine and reports use of Intel AMX instructions.

I believe the issue is related to OS or VM which (incorrectly) advertises support for Intel AMX via CPUID and XCR0, but fails to execute actual instructions.

After much internal investigation, root cause is github runner `windows-2025` for 5th gen Xeon EMR platform, advertises inconsistent CPUID AMX capabilities. Details at https://github.com/actions/runner-images/issues/14483
This causes [get_max_palette()](https://github.com/uxlfoundation/oneDNN/blob/b7bfe8bf3c252d31bcbf93d30b617897a1e447be/src/cpu/x64/cpu_isa_traits.cpp#L269) to return a 0 and at the same time, something like [amx_tile](https://github.com/uxlfoundation/oneDNN/blob/b7bfe8bf3c252d31bcbf93d30b617897a1e447be/src/cpu/x64/cpu_isa_traits.hpp#L466) case is true.
So, in my testing a `brgemm` test emits `palette_id = 0` from https://github.com/uxlfoundation/oneDNN/blob/b7bfe8bf3c252d31bcbf93d30b617897a1e447be/src/cpu/x64/brgemm/brgemm.cpp#L799
eventually calling `TILEZERO tmm0` which raises #UD.
Will wait https://github.com/actions/runner-images/issues/14483 to be resolved / addressed and reopen issue if needed.

PS -

- EMR runner reports AMX absent many times via cpuid.7 and xcr0, which is fine and does not create issues
- GNR reports AMX present and all cpuid bits are correct including cpuid.1d, so no problems there.

Thanks for thorough invsetigation, @rahulchaphalkar!

This looks like a hypervisor configuration bug. Though we may introduce a check for number of available palettes to prevent expensive investigations in the future.
